Hey there, what's going on today?
Hello. It is a fine day, how about yourself?
It really is! I am just taking in the fresh air in the backyard.
That is awesome.
Thanks! What is going on in your neck of the woods?
Sort of stuck inside trying to make a dime but it is alright.
Yeah great minds think alike.. do you do anything else for work?
Looking for a good job right now.
I wanted to talk about a personal issue I have been having, though.
Okay, you know I'm here for you. Talk to me, what's happening?
My father and I had a fight 2 years ago and haven't spoke since.
The same happened to me, and then my father passed away. If there is anything I can say, is to swallow pride and cherish the moments you have on earth together. What was the fight over?
Yeah I am afraid that these things can happen. It was only over material things.
That was my next question, what the fight was over. Do you think he would be open to mending things?
It is weird because I called him out for being manipulative so this is his defense.
Usually when people feel singled out, they only have a few mechanisms. Unfortunately, most people tend to run away instead of fixing things. It tends to be the easier option.
I would likely take advantage of an opportunity to be the bigger person.
When you try to fix things, just remember that this is his method. I wouldn't hold back on what you have to say, but just word it so that he doesn't feel the need to flee.
That is probably decent advice.
It is HIS responsibility as a parent to want to fix things, but you are also being the bigger person here. I applaud you and hope that he is receptive.
I hope so too, but the opportunity seems tenuous
How did you guys leave it?
Threatening and disparagement haha
Ha, well after two years, feelings had to have changed. Even a little. Does he live nearby?
Yeah someday. I think I will have to try you know. THanks for the advice.
Hey Charles, I'm here for you. How are you holding up after everything with Emily?
Hi, it's been really challenging. Seeing Emily in the hospital is something no parent wants.
I completely understand. It must be really hard to see her go through this. How is she doing now?
She's stable now, thankfully. But every time she has an episode, it takes a toll on us, especially Margaret.
I'm relieved to hear Emily is stable. The stress must be immense for you both. What's been the most difficult part?
I think it's the feeling of helplessness. We do everything we can, but it feels like we're just waiting for the next attack.
That sounds overwhelming, Charles. Feeling helpless is tough. Have you found anything that helps ease that feeling, even a little?
Talking to someone helps a bit. And knowing we're following the doctor’s advice, but the uncertainty lingers.
It's good that you're reaching out and following medical guidance. It's okay to feel uncertain; anyone would in your shoes.
Thanks, I appreciate that. Margaret tries to be strong for Emily, but I can see it's wearing her down too.
Margaret sounds like a wonderful mother, but it's important for both of you to care for yourselves too. How are you supporting each other?
We're trying to talk things out and give each other breaks. It's a work in progress.
That's a healthy approach. It's so important to lean on each other and take things one day at a time.
Yeah, some days are better than others. Getting back to a routine helps, but the worry is constant.
That constant worry must be exhausting. Do you have any outlets or activities to help manage it?
I try to go for a run in the mornings. It's not much, but it clears my head for a bit.
Exercise is great for stress relief. Even small moments of peace are valuable. You're doing your best, and that matters.
Thank you. It's good to hear that. It's just hard not to feel guilty for needing time away.
Taking care of yourself isn't selfish; it's necessary. Being at your best helps you support Emily and Margaret even better.
You're right. I need to remember that. It's a delicate balance, but we're getting there.

seeker: Hello. It is a fine day, how about yourself?

supporter: How did you guys leave it?

I completely understand. It must be really hard to see her go through this. How is she doing now?
She's stable now, thankfully. But every time she has an episode, it takes a toll on us, especially Margaret.
I'm relieved to hear Emily is stable. The stress must be immense for you both. What's been the most difficult part?
I think it's the feeling of helplessness. We do everything we can, but it feels like we're just waiting for the next attack.

We're trying to talk things out and give each other breaks. It's a work in progress.
That's a healthy approach. It's so important to lean on each other and take things one day at a time.
Yeah, some days are better than others. Getting back to a routine helps, but the worry is constant.
That constant worry must be exhausting. Do you have any outlets or activities to help manage it?
I try to go for a run in the mornings. It's not much, but it clears my head for a bit.
Exercise is great for stress relief. Even small moments of peace are valuable. You're doing your best, and that matters.
Thank you. It's good to hear that. It's just hard not to feel guilty for needing time away.
Taking care of yourself isn't selfish; it's necessary. Being at your best helps you support Emily and Margaret even better.
You're right. I need to remember that. It's a delicate balance, but we're getting there.
It sounds like you and Margaret are doing an incredible job under tough circumstances. Keep leaning on each other. You're not alone.
Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk things out and know someone understands.
Anytime, Charles. I'm here whenever you need to talk. You're doing great, just keep taking those steps forward.

Losing someone is never easy, especially when there are unresolved feelings. It's important to allow yourself to grieve and express those emotions. How’s it been opening up about that in therapy?
It was difficult at first, but slowly I'm learning to process the regret without letting it consume me.

Emily's health seems a bit better, which is a relief, but I still worry a lot. Margaret has been a rock, but I know she’s stressed too.

Hello. How are you feeling today?
Hi, I'm feeling really anxious today.
What has made you feel anxious?
Yesterday my company laid off 10% of the workforce and another 10% got furloughed.
I'm afraid I might be in the next round.
I am very sorry to hear that. I am currently in a situation where furloughs are greatly affecting my family as well.
Oh no that's terrible.
The problem is, I am right now the only breadwinner in the family. My wife was laid off three months ago
Are you given specifics on time of furlough?
No, it's basically until things get better.
I know that's very difficult. And no doubt why you're here working for crumbs.
It's why I'm here as well.
Yeah, trying to make ends meet wherever I can
I've been also trying to do uber as well but everyone is doing it also
I know it's a difficult time. Yes Uber is definitely overrun right now. Have you taken any time out to address your anxiety so it doesn't become more serious?
I don't know what I can do. I've been trying to keep busy. And I can't afford a therapist or anything like that.
Yes, that's definitely an expense you can't afford right now. But are you familiar with the concept of controlled breathing to help reduce or relieve anxiety?
Like meditation?
What am I supposed to do? Just breathe in and out a lot?

Not exactly. Controlled breathing is more of getting yourself into a quiet room. Closing your eyes, and purposely and intently focusing on your breathing. Slowly breathe in for a count of 5, then slowly exhale for a count of 5. Repeat this process for approximately 10 minute. It will help your stress levels and help regulate your heart rate!
Oh I didn't know that. No, I haven't tried that. Does it really work?
I've been using it myself over the past 3 months and it most definitely helps! But it's absolutely imperative to clear your mind and have complete quiet.
ok I can try it I guess
thanks for that tip
No problem. I hope this gives you some relief! Stay strong!
yeah, thanks. same to you

My final piece of advice would be to set aside time that is specified where nothing negative is discussed. No politics, no bills, nothing anxiety producing for you. It's probably best if this time is within an hour of your bedtime becuase anxiety is not conducive to a good night's sleep.
That's helpful. Thanks.
No problem. Take care. Wishing you well on your situation.
Thanks. You too

Hello. How are you feeling today?
Hi, I'm feeling really anxious today.
What has made you feel anxious?
Yesterday my company laid off 10% of the workforce and another 10% got furloughed.
I'm afraid I might be in the next round.
I am very sorry to hear that. I am currently in a situation where furloughs are greatly affecting my family as well.
Oh no that's terrible.
The problem is, I am right now the only breadwinner in the family. My wife was laid off three months ago
Are you given specifics on time of furlough?
No, it's basically until things get better.
I know that's very difficult. And no doubt why you're here working for crumbs.
It's why I'm here as well.
Yeah, trying to make ends meet wherever I can
I've been also trying to do uber as well but everyone is doing it also
I know it's a difficult time. Yes Uber is definitely overrun right now. Have you taken any time out to address your anxiety so it doesn't become more serious?
I don't know what I can do. I've been trying to keep busy. And I can't afford a therapist or anything like that.
Yes, that's definitely an expense you can't afford right now. But are you familiar with the concept of controlled breathing to help reduce or relieve anxiety?
Like meditation?
What am I supposed to do? Just breathe in and out a lot?

Not exactly. Controlled breathing is more of getting yourself into a quiet room. Closing your eyes, and purposely and intently focusing on your breathing. Slowly breathe in for a count of 5, then slowly exhale for a count of 5. Repeat this process for approximately 10 minute. It will help your stress levels and help regulate your heart rate!
Oh I didn't know that. No, I haven't tried that. Does it really work?
I've been using it myself over the past 3 months and it most definitely helps! But it's absolutely imperative to clear your mind and have complete quiet.
ok I can try it I guess
thanks for that tip
No problem. I hope this gives you some relief! Stay strong!
yeah, thanks. same to you

My final piece of advice would be to set aside time that is specified where nothing negative is discussed. No politics, no bills, nothing anxiety producing for you. It's probably best if this time is within an hour of your bedtime becuase anxiety is not conducive to a good night's sleep.
That's helpful. Thanks.
No problem. Take care. Wishing you well on your situation.
Thanks. You too

Hello. How are you feeling today?
Hi, I'm feeling really anxious today.
What has made you feel anxious?
Yesterday my company laid off 10% of the workforce and another 10% got furloughed.
I'm afraid I might be in the next round.
I am very sorry to hear that. I am currently in a situation where furloughs are greatly affecting my family as well.
Oh no that's terrible.
The problem is, I am right now the only breadwinner in the family. My wife was laid off three months ago
Are you given specifics on time of furlough?
No, it's basically until things get better.
I know that's very difficult. And no doubt why you're here working for crumbs.
It's why I'm here as well.
Yeah, trying to make ends meet wherever I can
I've been also trying to do uber as well but everyone is doing it also
I know it's a difficult time. Yes Uber is definitely overrun right now. Have you taken any time out to address your anxiety so it doesn't become more serious?
I don't know what I can do. I've been trying to keep busy. And I can't afford a therapist or anything like that.
Yes, that's definitely an expense you can't afford right now. But are you familiar with the concept of controlled breathing to help reduce or relieve anxiety?
Like meditation?
What am I supposed to do? Just breathe in and out a lot?

Hi Charles, how are things going with you lately?
Hey, things have been a bit overwhelming but also hopeful. Margaret just received a full-time job offer, which is great.
That sounds like a huge step forward! How does that make you feel?
I'm incredibly relieved and happy for her. It feels like we’re finally getting some stability back in our lives. But I also feel a bit anxious.
It makes sense to feel both relief and anxiety. What’s on your mind that's causing the anxiety?
I suppose it's the transition. I'm worried about how it'll change our family dynamics and whether Margaret and I can manage our time well.
Transitions can indeed be challenging. Have you discussed any plans or routines with Margaret to help manage these changes?
We've talked about a few things, especially around Emily’s care and our schedules. But there's still that lingering fear of the unknown.
The fear of the unknown can be tough. Remember, you two have navigated challenging times before and came out stronger.
Yes, that's true. We've been through a lot, and Margaret's job offer feels like a new beginning after those tough months.
It's definitely an opportunity for a fresh start. How's your job going, by the way?
It’s been positive. The new role is less stressful, and I’m reconnecting with colleagues. It’s been good for my mental health.
I’m so glad to hear that your job is going well. How have your therapy sessions been helping with everything?
Therapy's been instrumental, especially after finding my father's letter. It’s helped me make peace with his passing and focus on the present.
That's wonderful progress, Charles. It sounds like you're finding peace with your past and building for the future.
I’m trying. Margaret’s job offer gives us both a bit of security, which helps in focusing on what's important now.
Security is key. It's great that you both have more of that now. How’s Emily doing with everything?
Emily’s been doing quite well. Gardening together has been a wonderful escape for us, helping her with her asthma.
That’s such a lovely way to bond and deal with stress together. You all seem to be heading in a positive direction.
We’re optimistic. It feels like we're turning a page, and even though there are uncertainties, we have each other.
That’s a beautiful way to put it. Remember, you’re never alone in this journey. I’m here whenever you need to chat.
Thank you so much. I really appreciate having this space to share and feel supported.

Hey Charles, I'm here for you. How are you holding up after everything with Emily?
Hi, it's been really challenging. Seeing Emily in the hospital is something no parent wants.
I completely understand. It must be really hard to see her go through this. How is she doing now?
She's stable now, thankfully. But every time she has an episode, it takes a toll on us, especially Margaret.
I'm relieved to hear Emily is stable. The stress must be immense for you both. What's been the most difficult part?
I think it's the feeling of helplessness. We do everything we can, but it feels like we're just waiting for the next attack.
That sounds overwhelming, Charles. Feeling helpless is tough. Have you found anything that helps ease that feeling, even a little?
Talking to someone helps a bit. And knowing we're following the doctor’s advice, but the uncertainty lingers.
It's good that you're reaching out and following medical guidance. It's okay to feel uncertain; anyone would in your shoes.
Thanks, I appreciate that. Margaret tries to be strong for Emily, but I can see it's wearing her down too.
Margaret sounds like a wonderful mother, but it's important for both of you to care for yourselves too. How are you supporting each other?
We're trying to talk things out and give each other breaks. It's a work in progress.
That's a healthy approach. It's so important to lean on each other and take things one day at a time.
Yeah, some days are better than others. Getting back to a routine helps, but the worry is constant.
That constant worry must be exhausting. Do you have any outlets or activities to help manage it?
I try to go for a run in the mornings. It's not much, but it clears my head for a bit.
Exercise is great for stress relief. Even small moments of peace are valuable. You're doing your best, and that matters.
Thank you. It's good to hear that. It's just hard not to feel guilty for needing time away.
Taking care of yourself isn't selfish; it's necessary. Being at your best helps you support Emily and Margaret even better.
You're right. I need to remember that. It's a delicate balance, but we're getting there.
It sounds like you and Margaret are doing an incredible job under tough circumstances. Keep leaning on each other. You're not alone.
Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk things out and know someone understands.
Anytime, Charles. I'm here whenever you need to talk. You're doing great, just keep taking those steps forward.
Hi Jane, it's great to hear from you again. How have you been holding up?
Hi, it's been a bit rough lately. My car broke down and the repair costs are just... more than I can handle right now.
Oh no, I'm so sorry to hear that, Jane. That must be incredibly stressful, especially with everything else you've had to deal with recently.
It really is. I've been trying to manage, but the financial stress keeps piling up. I still haven't resolved the money issue with my friend, and now this... It's overwhelming.
I can only imagine how difficult that must be. You've been doing your best under such challenging circumstances. It's okay to feel overwhelmed.
Thank you. Sometimes it feels like I'm just not able to catch a break. I've been trying to keep track of everything with my journal, but it feels like every day brings something new.

Hey! How are you?
Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
Have you confronted him about it yet?
Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
Have you broken up yet?

No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't
I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)

I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with.
Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on

I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.

To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first

I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
Your welcome ;)
Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.

Hey Jane, how have you been holding up lately?
Hi. Not too great, to be honest. It's been a rough couple of weeks.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been going on?
Well, do you remember Lisa? My friend I mentioned before?
Yes, I remember you talking about them. What's up with Lisa?
So, we've hit this weird and stressful snag. I lent her some money months ago and she hasn’t paid me back yet.
That definitely sounds stressful. How is it affecting your relationship with Lisa?
She's completely cut off communication with me. No calls, texts, nothing.
That must be really hard on you, especially since she was such a close friend.
It feels like losing a part of my life. We used to hang out all the time and now it's just silence.
It sounds like you're mourning the loss of that friendship. Have you had a chance to reach out or communicate with her recently?
I’ve tried. Sent a couple of messages, but they’ve gone unanswered.
It must feel really disappointing not to hear back. What do you miss most about your friendship with Lisa?
We used to bounce ideas off each other, and she was the first person I'd call when something great happened at work.
It's understandable to miss those shared moments and support. How are you managing everything else alongside this?
It's made focusing on work tough. I feel a bit isolated, honestly.
I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. Feeling isolated can really weigh on you. Is there anyone else you feel comfortable confiding in?
I haven't really opened up to anyone else about this. It's been hard admitting to myself how deep this issue has affected me.
It takes a lot of courage to open up. It's important to take time for yourself and process everything. Is there anything you can do to help ease your mind a bit right now?
Maybe get back into some hobbies. I used to enjoy painting but haven't done it in a while.
That sounds like a wonderful idea. Engaging in something creative can be really therapeutic. Would you like support picking it back up?
I think that would help. Just getting started again might lift this weight a little.
I'm here to support you with this. Whenever you're ready, you can share your progress, and I’d love to hear how it goes.
Thank you. It feels a bit better knowing someone’s there to listen. I appreciate it.
Anytime, Jane. You’re not alone in this. We'll take it one step at a time.

Hey! How are you?
Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
Have you confronted him about it yet?
Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
Have you broken up yet?

No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't
I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)

I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with.
Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on

I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.

To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first

I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
Your welcome ;)
Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.

I attended a social event recently, and it unearthed some emotions I thought I had tucked away.

I met someone there who reminded me of my past relationships, particularly the one that ended in a mess due to infidelity.

It was like reliving a bit of that heartache. I was both fascinated and apprehensive.

Hey! How are you?
Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
Have you confronted him about it yet?
Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
Have you broken up yet?

No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't
I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)

I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with.
Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on

I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.

To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first

I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
Your welcome ;)
Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.

Well, do you remember Lisa? My friend I mentioned before?

Have you confronted him about it yet?
Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
Have you broken up yet?

No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't
I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.

yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better

Well I would say mentally because I frequently think about her and constantly have memories throughout the day. Also when i hear a certain song or see a restaurant it makes me think of her.
Memories are a blessing and a curse. Are the memories and thought you are  having positive or negative?
They are a mix of both because at one point they were positive and now when I think about it, it brings me down in a negative way.
What have you done in the past to help you move on from a break up?

It’s hard when we have various emotions. These memories being more negative are hard to cope with. In my experience, if I rethink memories regarding relationships which tend to bring me down in way that is a learning experience, I feel more empowered.
Yeah I agree that's what I have been doing too, and it's nice to know that you do the same.
In my past I have been able to try and look at each  relationship as a chance to grow. To figure out what worked with that person and what didn’t. I have them used this as a tool for the future.
That's a good way to look at it.
You are making good steps to rethink the situations. Is there anything else contributing to the heat rack you still feel?
Heartbreak
Well I have also not met anyone since and fear that I will not fall in love again.

That is difficult. I understand how it feels to be lonely. Something I’ve done when I’ve felt that way was to learn to fall in love with myself. I like to do self care and make time for things I might not have time for if I were in a relationship.
hmm interesting I have never thought about falling in love with myself..maybe I will give it a try. Thanks.
It’s so important to love yourself. Self love breeds confidence and confidence is not only attractive, but powerful in so many ways
I appreciate the feedback and support, you have helped me take the next step to move on with my life.
I’m glad I could help. You will overcome this.
Thank you and hope to talk to you again. Have a good night.
You too.

It was like my feelings didn't matter to them, and it made me question if they really care about me.","speaker":"seeker","start_char":0,"turn_index":6}],"kind":"ME","last_confirmed_at":null,"observed_outcome":null,"past_report":"felt down and questioned whether friends care after being dismissed during personal sharing","reported_at":"2024-08-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2"}
Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How's everything on your end?
Hey, not too great to be honest. I tried opening up to my friends at the gathering I hosted, but it didn't go as I hoped.
I'm sorry to hear that, Jimmy. It sounds frustrating. Do you want to talk more about what happened?
Yeah, I felt like I was finally ready to share some personal stuff, and it seemed like nobody wanted to listen or take it seriously.
That must have been really tough, especially when you were putting yourself out there. How did you end up feeling after that?
I felt pretty down. It was like my feelings didn't matter to them, and it made me question if they really care about me.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. It sounds like you were looking for some support from your friends.
Exactly. I just wanted someone to hear me out and maybe offer some advice or comfort.
Feeling dismissed by friends could be really disheartening. Have you experienced anything like this before with them?
Not really. That's why it was kind of a shock. I just didn't expect it from them.
That makes it even harder when it's unexpected. Was there anyone at the gathering who you felt did listen or understand?
I think one of my friends was trying, but got caught up in someone else’s conversation. It wasn’t like they ignored me on purpose.
It sounds like they had a lot going on at the time. But still, it's important that they realize how that affected you.
Yeah, I hope I can talk to them about how I felt. I'm just not sure how to bring it up without making it awkward.
It's definitely a delicate subject, but expressing how you feel is also important. Maybe you could start by mentioning how much their support means to you?
That's a good idea. I guess I could tell them that it would really mean a lot to me if they could be there for me when I need it.
That sounds like a thoughtful way to start the conversation. Remember, real friends will want to support you when they know something's up.
Thanks, I really appreciate that. It helps to talk it through and feel a bit more prepared.
Anytime, Jimmy. I'm here for you if you need to chat more. You're doing great by taking the steps to communicate how you feel.
Thanks, it means a lot. I'll let you know how it goes.
Hey Jimmy, how are you doing today?
Hey. It's been a rough day, to be honest.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How may I help you?
seeker: Hi I am feeling quite sad today.
supporter: Ohh, sorry to hear that. Any partucular reason?
seeker: Yes I feel like my friends just don't care about me much at all.
supporter: You saying that your friend does not care about you any more. Is that correct?
seeker: Yes, when we get together all they want to do is talk about themselves. When I raise something that is bothering me they just ignore what I say and go back to what they want to talk about.
supporter: That's not good. You must be feeling left out. 
seeker: Yes I feel left out and unsupported by them.
supporter: Any particular reason they are doing such thing?
seeker: Well I think they don't care about me and are just selfish about their needs.
supporter: In that case, should you consider them as your friends?
seeker: Well they are the only friends I have and I have known them a long time. Do you think I should stop being friends with them ?
supporter: If someone is not friendly they are not real friend. You need to find someone who will stand by you no matter what..
seeker: Oh well that makes me feel sad too.  I will be saying goodbye to some long friendships. Do you think that is the only answer ?
supporter: Ok.. how about hosting them in your place for a gettogether.. 
seeker: Ok how do you think that would help me ?
supporter: They might open up if you are hosting .. people are generally nice to the host.. 
seeker: Yes that is true, it's a good idea.  I could also take the opportunity to tell them how I am feeling.
supporter: Good.. let's try that.. Anythign else I could help you with?
seeker: No you have been very helpful and I feel much better now I have a plan of action to address my problem. Thanks.
supporter: Thank you .. have a good day.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

Yes I feel like my friends just don't care about me much at all.

Yes I feel left out and unsupported by them.

Well I think they don't care about me and are just selfish about their needs.

Well they are the only friends I have and I have known them a long time. Do you think I should stop being friends with them ?
If someone is not friendly they are not real friend. You need to find someone who will stand by you no matter what..
Oh well that makes me feel sad too.  I will be saying goodbye to some long friendships. Do you think that is the only answer ?
Ok.. how about hosting them in your place for a gettogether..
Ok how do you think that would help me ?
They might open up if you are hosting .. people are generally nice to the host..
Yes that is true, it's a good idea.  I could also take the opportunity to tell them how I am feeling.
Good.. let's try that.. Anythign else I could help you with?
No you have been very helpful and I feel much better now I have a plan of action to address my problem. Thanks.
Thank you .. have a good day.
Hey Jimmy, how are you doing today?
Hey. It's been a rough day, to be honest.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Jimmy, good to hear from you. How have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hi George. I've been okay, I guess. It's been a bit of a rollercoaster recently.
supporter: I get that. You've had a lot on your plate. What's been going on?
seeker: Well, I went to an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting for the first time yesterday.
supporter: That's a huge step, Jimmy. I'm really proud of you for taking it. How did it feel?
seeker: Intimidating, honestly. Walking in there, not knowing anyone, feeling vulnerable... it wasn't easy.
supporter: I can only imagine how tough that must have been. But you did it, and that says a lot about your courage.
seeker: Thanks, George. I kept thinking about that day at the gathering when I tried to talk to everyone but felt ignored.
supporter: I remember you mentioning that. It must've been so frustrating to feel unheard by people you consider friends.
seeker: Yeah, it was. I guess that's part of why I pushed myself to try something different, like the AA meeting.
supporter: That makes sense. It sounds like you’re finding new ways to address things that were weighing you down.
seeker: Yeah, I hope so. I just worry about the process, you know? What if I can't handle it?
supporter: It's normal to feel that way, Jimmy. Recovery is a journey, not a sprint. It's okay to have doubts.
seeker: I appreciate that. I do want to keep going, but the fear of failing is there.
supporter: Fear is natural, but remember you've already taken the first step. You have the support to go through this.
seeker: Thanks, that helps. The people at the meeting were welcoming, which made a difference.
supporter: That's really good to hear. It's important to feel supported and understood in a group like that.
seeker: Yeah, it felt different from trying to talk with my current friends. I think I need this new beginning.
supporter: It sounds like you're on the right path, Jimmy. I'm here for you, whatever you need.
seeker: That really means a lot to me, George. Thanks for being there.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

Hey Jimmy, how are you doing today?
Hey. It's been a rough day, to be honest.
I'm here for you. Do you want to talk about it?
Thanks. Yeah, I had a disagreement with my manager at work today.
That sounds frustrating. What happened?
We didn't see eye to eye on what should be prioritized. It just made me anxious.
Conflict like that can be really stressful. Did you get a chance to express your perspective?
I tried, but it felt like he wasn't really listening. It reminded me of when I felt ignored by friends before.
I remember you sharing that experience at the gathering you hosted. It's tough feeling sidelined.
Exactly. It feels like no matter where I turn, I'm not being heard.
It's disheartening when communication doesn't feel effective. Have you been able to talk to anyone else about this?
I did mention it to my new friend from the AA meetings. It helps having someone who gets the struggle.
It's great that you have that connection. How are things going with AA?
It's been eye-opening and comforting, but the work stress isn't helping.
Balancing everything can be challenging. Would you consider discussing this with your manager again with maybe different strategies in mind?
I've thought about it. Maybe writing down my points beforehand could help.
That sounds like a solid plan. It might help make sure you’re heard.
Thanks. I just need to find the courage to approach him again.
You have that courage, Jimmy. Remember how you stepped up to attend those AA meetings?
Yeah, you're right. If I did that, I can do this too.
Absolutely. You're stronger than you realize. I'm here to back you.
Thanks for saying that. It means a lot.
Anytime. Let me know how it goes, okay?
I will. Thanks again for listening.
Always here for you, Jimmy. Take care.
Hey Jimmy, how are you holding up today?
Not great, honestly. I had a fallout with George yesterday about my drinking.

Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How's everything on your end?
Hey, not too great to be honest. I tried opening up to my friends at the gathering I hosted, but it didn't go as I hoped.
I'm sorry to hear that, Jimmy. It sounds frustrating. Do you want to talk more about what happened?
Yeah, I felt like I was finally ready to share some personal stuff, and it seemed like nobody wanted to listen or take it seriously.
That must have been really tough, especially when you were putting yourself out there. How did you end up feeling after that?
I felt pretty down. It was like my feelings didn't matter to them, and it made me question if they really care about me.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. It sounds like you were looking for some support from your friends.
Exactly. I just wanted someone to hear me out and maybe offer some advice or comfort.
Feeling dismissed by friends could be really disheartening. Have you experienced anything like this before with them?
Not really. That's why it was kind of a shock. I just didn't expect it from them.
That makes it even harder when it's unexpected. Was there anyone at the gathering who you felt did listen or understand?
I think one of my friends was trying, but got caught up in someone else’s conversation. It wasn’t like they ignored me on purpose.
It sounds like they had a lot going on at the time. But still, it's important that they realize how that affected you.
Yeah, I hope I can talk to them about how I felt. I'm just not sure how to bring it up without making it awkward.
It's definitely a delicate subject, but expressing how you feel is also important. Maybe you could start by mentioning how much their support means to you?
That's a good idea. I guess I could tell them that it would really mean a lot to me if they could be there for me when I need it.
That sounds like a thoughtful way to start the conversation. Remember, real friends will want to support you when they know something's up.
Thanks, I really appreciate that. It helps to talk it through and feel a bit more prepared.
Anytime, Jimmy. I'm here for you if you need to chat more. You're doing great by taking the steps to communicate how you feel.
Thanks, it means a lot. I'll let you know how it goes.
Hey Jimmy, how are you holding up today?
Not great, honestly. I had a fallout with George yesterday about my drinking.

Hello
Hi there I was hoping you can help me.
Sure. What can I help you with?
Well you see I am heartbroken and I can't seem to move on from a previous relationship, and its been over two years. Do you have any advice?
I’m understand how hard ending a relationship can be.
What do you find is the hardest thing for you each day. That is, where do you find it hardest to move on?
Well I would say mentally because I frequently think about her and constantly have memories throughout the day. Also when i hear a certain song or see a restaurant it makes me think of her.
Memories are a blessing and a curse. Are the memories and thought you are  having positive or negative?
They are a mix of both because at one point they were positive and now when I think about it, it brings me down in a negative way.
What have you done in the past to help you move on from a break up?

It’s hard when we have various emotions. These memories being more negative are hard to cope with. In my experience, if I rethink memories regarding relationships which tend to bring me down in way that is a learning experience, I feel more empowered.
Yeah I agree that's what I have been doing too, and it's nice to know that you do the same.
In my past I have been able to try and look at each  relationship as a chance to grow. To figure out what worked with that person and what didn’t. I have them used this as a tool for the future.
That's a good way to look at it.
You are making good steps to rethink the situations. Is there anything else contributing to the heat rack you still feel?
Heartbreak
Well I have also not met anyone since and fear that I will not fall in love again.

That is difficult. I understand how it feels to be lonely. Something I’ve done when I’ve felt that way was to learn to fall in love with myself. I like to do self care and make time for things I might not have time for if I were in a relationship.
hmm interesting I have never thought about falling in love with myself..maybe I will give it a try. Thanks.
It’s so important to love yourself. Self love breeds confidence and confidence is not only attractive, but powerful in so many ways
I appreciate the feedback and support, you have helped me take the next step to move on with my life.
I’m glad I could help. You will overcome this.
Thank you and hope to talk to you again. Have a good night.
You too.
Hey Jimmy, how are you holding up today?
Not great, honestly. I had a fallout with George yesterday about my drinking.

Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How have the AA meetings been going?
Hey there. Well, surprisingly, they've been quite helpful. I met someone there, Bob, who's kind of going through the same issues.
That's great to hear. It must feel nice to have someone who truly understands what you're going through.
Yeah, definitely. It feels different from when I talked to my other friends. They just didn't get it, you know?
I remember you mentioned feeling dismissed by them before. It sounds like finding someone who empathizes really makes a difference.
Exactly. With Bob, I don't feel judged. We can share our stories, and it's like this unspoken bond.
That unspoken understanding can be so powerful. Have you been able to open up more because of it?
A bit. It's scary, but I’ve been sharing more of my feelings, and it feels freeing somehow. The fear of being judged or not being taken seriously is starting to fade.
That sounds like real progress, Jimmy. Have you felt any changes in your day-to-day life since attending these meetings?
Yeah, definitely. I've started to recognize some patterns in my behavior and why I turned to alcohol. It's frightening to see, but it’s the first step, I guess.
Acknowledging those patterns is a huge step. It's brave of you to face those issues head-on.
Thanks. I just sometimes worry if I’m too late, you know? That I might lose everything.
It's normal to feel that way, but you’re taking action now, and that’s important. It's never too late to make a change.
Yeah, you're right. I guess I just have to keep reminding myself of that.
Absolutely. And remember, you're not alone in this. Bob and others at AA are there for you, and so am I.
I appreciate that. It's comforting to have a supportive net. I need to hold onto that.
You're building a strong foundation, Jimmy. Just keep taking it one day at a time.
Thanks. It helps to break it down like that. I’ll try to focus on each day and not get overwhelmed.
That sounds like a solid plan. You've got this, Jimmy. Remember, progress is progress, no matter how small.
Thanks a lot. Your words mean a lot to me right now. I’ll keep them in mind.
Anytime. I'm here whenever you need to talk. Keep me posted on how things go, okay?
I will. Thanks again, really. I'll talk to you soon.
Hi Jimmy, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster. I'm trying something new with mindfulness and meditation.
That's interesting! What made you decide to explore mindfulness and meditation?
I just felt really overwhelmed after everything that happened recently. My anxiety has been through the roof.
I can imagine. It sounds like you've been through a lot. How have the mindfulness exercises been for you so far?
It's still new, but I think it's helping a bit. I can, at least, find moments of calm when I focus on it.
That's great to hear, even small moments of relief can be a huge step forward. Have you found any particular techniques that work well for you?
Guided meditations seem to work best, especially those focusing on anxiety. It's like having a support system even when alone.
It sounds like a very constructive approach. Have your interactions with Bob from the AA meetings been helpful as well?
Yeah, Bob's been really supportive. It feels good to have someone who truly gets it.

Work has been tense. Got a warning over attendance, which just adds to the anxiety, you know?
That sounds really tough, especially when you're dealing with so much. Are you finding any ways to manage the stress related to work?
I'm trying to focus on what's directly in front of me and not let my mind wander. But at the same time, those past arguments with my manager still haunt me.
It's understandable. Past conflicts can linger, but it's great that you're focusing on the present tasks. Maybe addressing these feelings with a professional could also be beneficial?
You might be right, seeking professional advice could help make sense of this tangled mess.
Absolutely, a therapist could offer strategies specifically tailored for you. How do you feel about that idea?
It feels daunting, opening up to someone new, but necessary if I want to move forward.

Hey. It's been a rough day, to be honest.
I'm here for you. Do you want to talk about it?
Thanks. Yeah, I had a disagreement with my manager at work today.
That sounds frustrating. What happened?
We didn't see eye to eye on what should be prioritized. It just made me anxious.
Conflict like that can be really stressful. Did you get a chance to express your perspective?
I tried, but it felt like he wasn't really listening. It reminded me of when I felt ignored by friends before.
I remember you sharing that experience at the gathering you hosted. It's tough feeling sidelined.
Exactly. It feels like no matter where I turn, I'm not being heard.

Anytime. Let me know how it goes, okay?
I will. Thanks again for listening.
Always here for you, Jimmy. Take care.

Hey. Honestly, not too well. I had a bit of a slip up recently.
I'm really sorry to hear that, Jimmy. Do you feel like talking about what happened?
Yeah, I guess it's better to talk about it. I was at a family gathering and it just got overwhelming... and I ended up drinking.
Family gatherings can definitely be tough. What do you think made it overwhelming for you?
It was just a lot, you know? Everyone kept asking about my job, and there was a lot of pressure to 'act normal.' I tried to keep it together, but it felt like suffocating.

Honestly, I felt ashamed. But I reached out to Bob, my new friend from the AA meetings, and they were pretty supportive about it.

A bit better. They reminded me that recovery isn't about being perfect; it's about trying to improve one step at a time.
That's a really healthy perspective. It's important to be gentle with yourself through this process. How else can I support you right now?
I'm just trying to figure out how to communicate better with my manager and deal with work stress. Bob suggested a couple of strategies.
That's a good step. Improving that relationship could lessen some of your stress. Do you feel like talking about those strategies?
Bob mentioned setting clearer boundaries and maybe considering mediation if things don't improve. It's nerve-racking, but I know I have to do something.

I've also thought about re-evaluating my workload to manage it better. Maybe take some time to plan rather than just react.

Hello
Hi there I was hoping you can help me.
Sure. What can I help you with?
Well you see I am heartbroken and I can't seem to move on from a previous relationship, and its been over two years. Do you have any advice?
I’m understand how hard ending a relationship can be.
What do you find is the hardest thing for you each day. That is, where do you find it hardest to move on?
Well I would say mentally because I frequently think about her and constantly have memories throughout the day. Also when i hear a certain song or see a restaurant it makes me think of her.
Memories are a blessing and a curse. Are the memories and thought you are  having positive or negative?
They are a mix of both because at one point they were positive and now when I think about it, it brings me down in a negative way.
What have you done in the past to help you move on from a break up?

Yeah I agree that's what I have been doing too, and it's nice to know that you do the same.
In my past I have been able to try and look at each  relationship as a chance to grow. To figure out what worked with that person and what didn’t. I have them used this as a tool for the future.
That's a good way to look at it.
You are making good steps to rethink the situations. Is there anything else contributing to the heat rack you still feel?
Heartbreak
Well I have also not met anyone since and fear that I will not fall in love again.

That is difficult. I understand how it feels to be lonely. Something I’ve done when I’ve felt that way was to learn to fall in love with myself. I like to do self care and make time for things I might not have time for if I were in a relationship.
hmm interesting I have never thought about falling in love with myself..maybe I will give it a try. Thanks.

Hey, I found something today while packing and it's kind of messing with my head.
I'm here for you, Jimmy. What did you find?
I stumbled upon an old letter from my ex-girlfriend. It brought back a lot of memories and feelings I thought I had moved past.
I can only imagine how overwhelming that must be. Do you want to talk about what those memories are bringing up for you?
It's just… it made me realize how much I've been trying to escape certain feelings instead of dealing with them.
That sounds like a powerful reflection, Jimmy. It’s never easy to confront past emotions. What’s been the hardest part for you about this realization?
It's the regret, I think. Regret about how things ended, and feeling like maybe a part of me hasn’t truly grown since then.
Regret can be tough to sit with. It sounds like you're questioning if you've made the progress you hoped for.
Yeah, and it makes me worry about whether I’ll just repeat my mistakes with Emily or keep stagnating in other parts of my life.
It’s understandable to feel that way given your recent journey. You've been working hard on yourself, though. Remember how far you've come since starting those AA meetings.
True, attending those meetings has helped. It just feels like there’s always this shadow of doubt following me.
Doubt can often linger, but it's also a sign that you're questioning and reflecting, which is a part of growth. Do you think the move to Sydney will help with some of these feelings?
I hope so. I see it as a step towards a new beginning, yet there's a fear that I might carry the same emotional baggage there.
It's natural to be worried about taking your past with you, but sometimes a change of scenery can offer a fresh perspective and reset.
That's what I'm banking on. Just hoping I can leave behind these old habits and finally start anew.
I believe you have the strength to make positive changes, Jimmy. You've shown a lot of resilience already. What’s one thing you’re looking forward to in Sydney?
Probably the chance to reinvent myself, meet new people, and maybe discover parts of Sydney I’ve not considered before.
That sounds like an exciting opportunity. You've got a world of possibilities ahead, and I'll be here to support you along the way.
Thanks, that means a lot. I guess time will tell how things unfold, but it’s reassuring to know I’m not facing this alone.
Absolutely, Jimmy. You’re not alone, and you’ve got a network of support that’s rooting for you. Keep us updated on how things go, okay?
I will. Thanks for listening, it’s helped put things in perspective.
Anytime, Jimmy. Take care of yourself while you’re packing, and remember to take things one day at a time.

Wow, that's very hard. I would be anxious too.

Hey Michael, how’s everything going with you today?

I got a job offer. Normally, that would be good news, but it's not as great as it sounds.
Oh really? What's got you feeling hesitant about it?
Well, it’s far from where I live, in a completely different area, and the pay is pretty low.
That sounds really challenging. Moving and taking a pay cut are big decisions. What are your main concerns?
Mainly, it's about leaving behind what little network I have here and starting over somewhere else for something that doesn’t seem worth it.
Leaving familiar places and people can be really tough. It makes sense that you'd feel conflicted.

I'm really glad you did. Remember, you're not alone in this. We'll figure it out together.

Good evening
Hello. How are you?
ok. How can I be of service tonight
I'm just feeling sad and depressed over the breakup that I described above. Hoping for some inspiration.
Tell me more please I am all ears
I feel so betrayed. I was completely caught off guard. Now I don't know what to do with myself.
When did this happen, How long ago
Just this last week. I came home from work early Thursday. I guess I should have texted first so he could get rid of the guy. Or maybe not. Maybe it's better that I found out.
So you had been together for awhile and all of  a sudden he has another person in his life
We were together almost ten years. Over nine and a half. I had no idea. I don't think the guy is even someone he really cares about. I don't know.
Was this guy an associate of yours as well
So basically this guy was a stranger that you know of.
Yes that's right, I'd never seen him before.
Did you have any children between you
No, it was just the two of us. And two cats. Who are still here with me. There's that at least.
DiId your partner work also
Just from home. Self-published author, some online work, stuff like that. He made about as much as I did, I wasn't the sole breadwinner or anything.
Maybe the time on his hands enabled to him meet someone while you were working. Did he have a following that you knew of
has there been habits like this before

Maybe it did. There are some fans of his work on social media, and he's on all the popular social media sights. I don't know if he me the guy online or what. There hasn't been anything like this before that I know of. Maybe there was. I trusted him and didn't look at his messages or anything.
His actions none the less are not right
Do you have an idea his websites
No, they weren't, I agree there. He took all his devices with him. I can see his stuff from a user point of view, like anyone else in the public could, but nothing of his personal stuff.
The fact that he cheated on you and I assume you broke up with him is hard
He must have a special account that people can access to, can you possibly find it out
Yeah, we're over. And it is hard. I'll get past it I suppose. I don't think I could, but I don't really want to anyway at this point. It's not going to help us get back together or anything.
Maybe you need to focus on you now, and plan your days ahead.
I think you're right. Just look forward.
Had you known before hand it might be of help, but the sudden impact does not make it any better
if you look back you will have regrets. If you look forward you will see a future
You're right. Thank you for listening. I feel a little better already. I'll get through this. Me and the cats :-)
Take a cup of coffee, sit and write your thoughts then burn them
Sounds like a good plan.
Write your past down then throw it into a fire
Thank you again. I'm going to go ahead and wrap up the conversation. I'll be okay.
OK. Have a blessed night.
You too. Take care.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, can I talk to you about something that's been on my mind?
supporter: Of course, Sarah. What's been happening?
seeker: I found out recently that my close friend has been dealing with depression, and it's really worrying me.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must be difficult to know someone you care about is struggling. How are you handling it?
seeker: Honestly, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed. I want to help but I'm not sure how.
supporter: Wanting to support your friend shows how much you care. It's okay not to have all the answers. Have you been able to talk to them about it?
seeker: We talked a little. They admitted things have been tough but didn’t go into much detail. I don’t want to push them.
supporter: It's great that they opened up to you a bit. Listening can be very supportive too. Have you been able to share some of what you're feeling with your therapist?
seeker: Yeah, I mentioned it in therapy, but I feel guilty for focusing on my own feelings when my friend is the one struggling.
supporter: Your feelings are valid too, Sarah. It’s natural to feel for your friend, but taking care of yourself is important. It helps you to be there for them.
seeker: That makes sense. I guess I'm just scared of making things worse, you know?
supporter: That’s a common fear, but being there for your friend and offering a listening ear can do a lot of good. Have you noticed any changes in how you both interact since you found out?
seeker: I’m trying to be more present when we're together. I feel like they've become more withdrawn, and it hurts to see.
supporter: It's tough seeing someone you care about in pain. But showing up and letting them know they're not alone is supportive.
seeker: I’ll keep that in mind. I just wish there was more I could do.
supporter: Your friend is lucky to have someone as caring as you. When you're ready, maybe suggesting they talk to a professional could help.
seeker: That’s a good point. Maybe I'll bring it up gently if the time feels right. It just feels like there’s so much to balance between work, therapy, and now worrying about my friend.
supporter: It's a lot to juggle, for sure. Remember, you're not alone in this. How has work been since you started therapy?
seeker: It's gotten better, slowly. I’m trying to set boundaries and leave work at the office.
supporter: That sounds like progress. It's so important to set boundaries for your well-being. Do you feel therapy has helped you in that regard?
seeker: Definitely. Having someone to talk to about these things has been grounding. I just need to remind myself to practice what I'm learning.
supporter: It's wonderful to hear therapy is helping. Implementing what you’ve learned can take time, so be patient with yourself.
seeker: Thanks. I’ll try to be kinder to myself. I really appreciate you listening and offering advice.
supporter: Anytime, Sarah. Remember, you're doing your best, and that counts for a lot. Don't hesitate to reach out again if you need to talk.
seeker: Thanks again. I’ll definitely reach out. Take care.

I'm feeling a mix of excitement and worry. It's great to be with someone I connect with, but I'm also scared about how things might change at work.
It's understandable to have those mixed feelings. Entering a new relationship is exciting but can also bring changes. What's your biggest concern right now?
I guess I'm worried about how our colleagues might react. We both agreed to keep things professional, but gossip can be brutal.
Office dynamics can be tricky. It sounds like you two have a good plan in place to stay professional. Do you think there's someone in the office you can confide in if things get challenging?
I do have a couple of colleagues who I trust. It's just that my last breakdown at work left me feeling a bit vulnerable. I'm trying to avoid that happening again.
It's great you have people you trust. And remember, you’ve come a long way since that incident. How have you been managing stress since starting therapy?
Therapy has been really helpful. It's taught me ways to set boundaries and be more open about my feelings. I think it’s why I felt ready to approach my colleague.
That's wonderful to hear. Taking those steps for personal growth can really make a difference. Have you talked to your therapist about starting this new relationship?
Not yet, but I'm planning on bringing it up in my next session. My therapist has really helped me gain perspective on my relationships.
That sounds like a great idea. Having professional guidance can really clarify things. How are things on the friendship front with your close friend?
My friend is still struggling, which has been hard to watch. I've been trying to be there for them without overstepping.
It must be tough to see someone you care about go through a hard time. How are you handling being supportive without taking on too much yourself?
I try to listen and offer support when I can but also remind myself that their journey is separate from mine, and I need to set limits for my own well-being.
That's a healthy approach. Remember, you can only do so much, and caring for yourself is crucial. How do you unwind after emotionally exhausting days?
I've been getting into yoga and reading a lot lately. It helps me center myself and escape my thoughts for a while.

Good evening
Hello. How are you?
ok. How can I be of service tonight
I'm just feeling sad and depressed over the breakup that I described above. Hoping for some inspiration.
Tell me more please I am all ears
I feel so betrayed. I was completely caught off guard. Now I don't know what to do with myself.
When did this happen, How long ago
Just this last week. I came home from work early Thursday. I guess I should have texted first so he could get rid of the guy. Or maybe not. Maybe it's better that I found out.
So you had been together for awhile and all of  a sudden he has another person in his life
We were together almost ten years. Over nine and a half. I had no idea. I don't think the guy is even someone he really cares about. I don't know.
Was this guy an associate of yours as well
So basically this guy was a stranger that you know of.
Yes that's right, I'd never seen him before.
Did you have any children between you
No, it was just the two of us. And two cats. Who are still here with me. There's that at least.
DiId your partner work also
Just from home. Self-published author, some online work, stuff like that. He made about as much as I did, I wasn't the sole breadwinner or anything.
Maybe the time on his hands enabled to him meet someone while you were working. Did he have a following that you knew of
has there been habits like this before

Maybe it did. There are some fans of his work on social media, and he's on all the popular social media sights. I don't know if he me the guy online or what. There hasn't been anything like this before that I know of. Maybe there was. I trusted him and didn't look at his messages or anything.
His actions none the less are not right
Do you have an idea his websites
No, they weren't, I agree there. He took all his devices with him. I can see his stuff from a user point of view, like anyone else in the public could, but nothing of his personal stuff.
The fact that he cheated on you and I assume you broke up with him is hard
He must have a special account that people can access to, can you possibly find it out
Yeah, we're over. And it is hard. I'll get past it I suppose. I don't think I could, but I don't really want to anyway at this point. It's not going to help us get back together or anything.
Maybe you need to focus on you now, and plan your days ahead.
I think you're right. Just look forward.
Had you known before hand it might be of help, but the sudden impact does not make it any better
if you look back you will have regrets. If you look forward you will see a future
You're right. Thank you for listening. I feel a little better already. I'll get through this. Me and the cats :-)
Take a cup of coffee, sit and write your thoughts then burn them
Sounds like a good plan.
Write your past down then throw it into a fire
Thank you again. I'm going to go ahead and wrap up the conversation. I'll be okay.
OK. Have a blessed night.
You too. Take care.

Hello! How are you doing today?
I'm good thanks but pretty frustrated too be honest. It's my friend who has taken to being a pain on Facebook
I'm sorry to hear you are frustrated! I'm gonna do my best to understand and talk through your issue. :) Your friend is being a pain on face book in what way?
He's all of a sudden got an opinion on everything and tries to pull me into arguments with other friends.
It sounds like he didn't use to blast his opinion in the past or include you in arguments, is that true?

That is true yes. It's like the world has to listen to his opinion and only his matters and he won't listen to reason. It's very frustrating and it makes me not want to talk to him. My eyes literally roll when I see a post from him.

Oh I see! I get where you are coming from. I have a few friends that no matter how long you discuss, they won't let the conversation end unless "they are right." It seems like your friend doesn't like it when he is wrong?
Absolutely and I'm not sure how to broach this with him. I actually feel like it is damaging his reputation. Other friends of ours feel the same way. Not sure what to do?

Gotcha so not only are you frustrated with what he is doing, but you are also worried about his reputation! First of all, can I ask if he is just your friend online or if you hangout with him in person too?
That's correct. He is actually a close friend and I wonder what has changed recently to make him like this. I've known him for over 20 years.

Okay I see. From personal experience, the best way to confront someone who likes to do most of their confrontations online, is in person. Since he is so used to almost "hiding" behind a screen, his feelings will be more vulnerable and real if you discuss your concerns in person.
Actually I've never thought of it like that. Perhaps a couple of us can have a conversation with him in person. Honestly some off his views are disgusting. I think this needs to stop.

A suggestion I would make would be to hangout with him in person, and bring up the issues that you and your friends have been seeing. But it's important to not make him feel overwhelmed. Almost like he is being "ganged up on."
Yes that's good advice, I think we need to be tactful and raise it in the right way. Have you ever experienced something like this with a friend yourself?

I can tell that you care about this person as a friend, but you are worried that the way he thinks and talks may ruin that in a way. Make sure to let him know these concerns! It will show him that you guys truly are doing it out of love.
And yes I have actually had a very similar experience! Let me explain
Ok sure please do

One of my best friend's and roommate, had a very hard time separating friendship and roommate issues. It caused a lot of issues in the relationships with our friends. She had a tendency to discuss issues over text and didn't like doing it in person. But we realized, the problem with that is that you can't tell the emotion behind messages on a screen. But once we talked in person, our issues were solved because we could hear the intended emotions behind what we were saying

Yeah that's useful. I think you are right in that the ambiguity of social interaction online makes him more inclined to say extreme thinks, perhaps to get a reaction. The more I think about it, perhaps this could be an indication that there is something he is dealing with and may be lashing out.

Yes exactly. It sounds like he might have other reasonings behind his actions. And you guys talking to him as friends in person, would show him that you care and that he is in a safe environment. He doesn't need to be so extreme
Yeah I think that's definitely the way forward. Listen this has really helped so thanks for the suggestions and sharing your own experiences.
Yes of course! I wish you the best in overcoming this hard time with your friend. I believe that you guys will be able to talk through it since it's a newer issue. :)
I hope so too. Nice to talk to you and thanks again.
Of course! Have a good rest of your day
Thanks

Of course, Sarah. What's been happening?
I found out recently that my close friend has been dealing with depression, and it's really worrying me.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must be difficult to know someone you care about is struggling. How are you handling it?
Honestly, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed. I want to help but I'm not sure how.
Wanting to support your friend shows how much you care. It's okay not to have all the answers. Have you been able to talk to them about it?
We talked a little. They admitted things have been tough but didn’t go into much detail. I don’t want to push them.
It's great that they opened up to you a bit. Listening can be very supportive too. Have you been able to share some of what you're feeling with your therapist?
Yeah, I mentioned it in therapy, but I feel guilty for focusing on my own feelings when my friend is the one struggling.
Your feelings are valid too, Sarah. It’s natural to feel for your friend, but taking care of yourself is important. It helps you to be there for them.
That makes sense. I guess I'm just scared of making things worse, you know?
That’s a common fear, but being there for your friend and offering a listening ear can do a lot of good. Have you noticed any changes in how you both interact since you found out?
I’m trying to be more present when we're together. I feel like they've become more withdrawn, and it hurts to see.
It's tough seeing someone you care about in pain. But showing up and letting them know they're not alone is supportive.

Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's been going on?

That's a big step! How are you feeling about it?
I'm feeling a mix of excitement and worry. It's great to be with someone I connect with, but I'm also scared about how things might change at work.

Anytime, Sarah. I'm here whenever you need to chat. Take care of yourself, okay?
I will. Thanks again!

Hi. I've been trying to find ways to manage my stress. My therapist suggested taking up a hobby, so I started painting.
That's wonderful! How has painting been for you?
It's been surprisingly soothing. There's something calming about watching the colors blend on the canvas. I didn't realize how much I needed this creative outlet.
It's amazing how art can have that effect. Do you find it helps with some of the stress from work and your personal life?
Definitely. Work has been overwhelming, especially after that meeting with my new boss. Painting helps me disconnect for a while.
I'm really glad to hear that it's providing a little escape. Has it also helped with your feelings of anxiety and the challenges you're facing with Jack?

I'd love to hear about your travels when they happen. For now, I'm here if you ever want to share more of your art journey or anything else.
Thank you for listening and being here. It means a lot to know I have support while I figure things out.
Anytime, Sarah. Keep painting and taking small steps. You're doing great.

Honestly, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed. I want to help but I'm not sure how.
Wanting to support your friend shows how much you care. It's okay not to have all the answers. Have you been able to talk to them about it?
We talked a little. They admitted things have been tough but didn’t go into much detail. I don’t want to push them.
It's great that they opened up to you a bit. Listening can be very supportive too. Have you been able to share some of what you're feeling with your therapist?
Yeah, I mentioned it in therapy, but I feel guilty for focusing on my own feelings when my friend is the one struggling.
Your feelings are valid too, Sarah. It’s natural to feel for your friend, but taking care of yourself is important. It helps you to be there for them.
That makes sense. I guess I'm just scared of making things worse, you know?
That’s a common fear, but being there for your friend and offering a listening ear can do a lot of good. Have you noticed any changes in how you both interact since you found out?
I’m trying to be more present when we're together. I feel like they've become more withdrawn, and it hurts to see.
It's tough seeing someone you care about in pain. But showing up and letting them know they're not alone is supportive.
I’ll keep that in mind. I just wish there was more I could do.
Your friend is lucky to have someone as caring as you. When you're ready, maybe suggesting they talk to a professional could help.
That’s a good point. Maybe I'll bring it up gently if the time feels right. It just feels like there’s so much to balance between work, therapy, and now worrying about my friend.
It's a lot to juggle, for sure. Remember, you're not alone in this. How has work been since you started therapy?
It's gotten better, slowly. I’m trying to set boundaries and leave work at the office.
That sounds like progress. It's so important to set boundaries for your well-being. Do you feel therapy has helped you in that regard?
Definitely. Having someone to talk to about these things has been grounding. I just need to remind myself to practice what I'm learning.
It's wonderful to hear therapy is helping. Implementing what you’ve learned can take time, so be patient with yourself.
Thanks. I’ll try to be kinder to myself. I really appreciate you listening and offering advice.
Anytime, Sarah. Remember, you're doing your best, and that counts for a lot. Don't hesitate to reach out again if you need to talk.
Thanks again. I’ll definitely reach out. Take care.
You too, take care.
